title: Who is your group's leader?
hook: Are these two people in the same group? You do not have to ask everyone.

doesNotKnow: how a program answers 'are these two already connected?' quickly

misconception: To check whether two people are in the same group you have to trace through everyone.
objective: The learner can explain that if each group is a tree under a leader and the smaller group always hangs under the bigger group's leader, nobody among 8 people is more than 3 hops from their leader, because a person only gets one hop further when their group at least doubles.

claims.text: With 8 people, hanging the smaller group under the bigger group's leader, nobody ends more than 3 hops from their leader; merging equal groups in pairs reaches exactly 3.
claims.source: Union by size bounds tree height by floor(log2 n) = 3 for n = 8 (see c3). Pairing merges (1+1, 2+2, 4+4) give height 3, shown by the stage's 'tallest way' button. CLRS 3rd ed. 21.3; exercise 21.4-2.

claims.text: In 1,000 random merge orders the worst tree was 3 hops tall.
claims.source: Stage button and builder's uf.mjs: random pairs of people (mulberry32 seed 1, not chosen; the first seed tried) until one group: worst height 3 (heights 1: 157, 2: 833, 3: 10). Also 20,000 orders at seed 7: worst 3.

claims.text: A person moves one hop further from their leader only when their group joins one at least as big, so their group at least doubles; from 1 to 8 that can happen only 3 times.
claims.source: A node's depth grows by 1 only when its root is hung under another root of a group at least as large, so its group size at least doubles; sizes go 1 -> at most 8, so at most log2 8 = 3 doublings. CLRS 3rd ed. 21.3-21.4.

recall.question: 1,024 people are merged into groups, always hanging the smaller group's leader under the bigger group's leader. At most how many hops is anyone from their leader?
recall.why: A person only moves a hop further when their group at least doubles, and 1 can double only 10 times before reaching 1,024 (2^10).
